_comment: The QAIRT/QNN runtime files RunAnywhere redistributes with the QHexRT engine.
RunAnywhere is an authorized Qualcomm partner; these are shipped under that agreement.
THIS IS THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for that file list. It previously lived in four
places that had already diverged: build-core-android.sh's qnn_host_libs/qnn_skel_libs,
bindings/kotlin/scripts/package-qhexrt.sh's QHEXRT_HOST_LIBS/QHEXRT_SKEL_LIBS, the
Electron flat staging dir, and the per-SDK jniLibs. A file added to one and not the
others fails a build with a name the other lists never mention.
Paths are relative to a QAIRT SDK root (the directory containing sdk.yaml).
The engine compiles against QAIRT HEADERS ONLY and dlopens these at runtime, so
shipping them beside the engine is packaging, not linking.
QAIRT-ROOT-SHAPED: build-core-android.sh reads lib/aarch64-android/ and
lib/hexagon-v<N>/unsigned/ from a QAIRT root and verifies identity by hashing
<root>/sdk.yaml. The layout and sdk.yaml are both load-bearing.
Skels are extracted on device and reached via ADSP_LIBRARY_PATH, so they stay
in their own directories rather than being flattened.
FLAT, and that is not a convenience: Windows has no ADSP_LIBRARY_PATH, so the
loader resolves the HTP stub's dependencies through the DLL's own directory and
every file must sit in ONE directory.
The .cat catalog is MANDATORY -- without it the skel fails signature verification
and the error never names the catalog.
Consumed via RA_QNN_RUNTIME_DIR by bindings/electron/scripts/bundle-native.ts.
